raw: Act 1, Scene 4 — A Street

sentences.en: A Street
sentences.ko: 거리

summary.en: Romeo and his friends go to the Capulet party in masks. Mercutio makes fun of Romeo's dreams, but Romeo feels that something bad will happen.
summary.ko: 로미오와 친구들이 가면을 쓰고 캐퓰릿 가의 잔치에 간다. 머큐쇼는 로미오의 꿈을 놀리지만, 로미오는 무언가 나쁜 일이 일어날 것만 같다.

raw: Enter Romeo, Mercutio, Benvolio, with five or six Maskers; Torch-bearers and others.

sentences.en: Romeo, Mercutio, and Benvolio enter.
sentences.ko: 로미오, 머큐쇼, 그리고 벤볼리오가 들어온다.

sentences.en: They are with five or six people in masks.
sentences.ko: 그들은 가면을 쓴 다섯 혹은 여섯 명과 함께 있다.

sentences.en: There are also torch-bearers and others.
sentences.ko: 횃불을 든 사람들과 다른 이들도 있다.

speaker: ROMEO
raw:
What, shall this speech be spoke for our excuse?
Or shall we on without apology?

sentences.en: Will we use this speech as our excuse?
sentences.ko: 준비한 인사말을 핑계 삼아 들어갈까?

sentences.en: Or should we just go on without an apology?
sentences.ko: 아니면 사과도 없이 그냥 들어갈까?

speaker: BENVOLIO
raw:
The date is out of such prolixity:
We’ll have no Cupid hoodwink’d with a scarf,
Bearing a Tartar’s painted bow of lath,
Scaring the ladies like a crow-keeper;
Nor no without-book prologue, faintly spoke
After the prompter, for our entrance:
But let them measure us by what they will,
We’ll measure them a measure, and be gone.

sentences.en: Such long speeches are out of fashion.
sentences.ko: 그런 긴 연설은 이제 유행이 아니야.

sentences.en: We will not have a boy dressed as a blindfolded Cupid.
sentences.ko: 눈을 가린 큐피드 분장을 한 소년은 필요 없어.

sentences.en: He would carry a painted wooden bow.
sentences.ko: 그는 색칠된 나무 활을 들고 있을 거야.

sentences.en: He would scare the ladies like a scarecrow.
sentences.ko: 그 애는 허수아비처럼 여자들을 겁주기나 할 거야.

sentences.en: We do not need a memorized speech, spoken weakly, for our entrance.
sentences.ko: 우리가 등장할 때 힘없이 외우는 대사를 할 필요는 없어.

sentences.en: Let them judge us however they want.
sentences.ko: 사람들이 우리를 어떻게 보든 상관없어.

sentences.en: We will dance one dance with them and then leave.
sentences.ko: 함께 한 곡 춤을 추고 나서 떠나자.

speaker: ROMEO
raw:
Give me a torch, I am not for this ambling;
Being but heavy I will bear the light.

sentences.en: Give me a torch.
sentences.ko: 횃불을 내놔.

sentences.en: I am not in the mood for dancing.
sentences.ko: 나는 춤출 기분이 아니야.

sentences.en: Since I am sad, I will carry the light.
sentences.ko: 나는 마음이 무거우니, 횃불이나 들게.

speaker: MERCUTIO
raw: Nay, gentle Romeo, we must have you dance.

sentences.en: No, gentle Romeo, we must have you dance.
sentences.ko: 안 돼, 다정한 로미오, 너도 꼭 춤을 춰야 해.

speaker: ROMEO
raw:
Not I, believe me, you have dancing shoes,
With nimble soles, I have a soul of lead
So stakes me to the ground I cannot move.

sentences.en: Believe me, I will not dance.
sentences.ko: 믿어줘, 난 절대 안 출 거야.

sentences.en: You have dancing shoes with thin soles.
sentences.ko: 너는 밑창이 얇은 춤용 신발을 신고 있잖아.

sentences.en: I have a soul of lead.
sentences.ko: 내 영혼은 납덩이 같아.

sentences.en: It holds me to the ground so I cannot move.
sentences.ko: 그게 나를 땅에 붙잡고 있어서 움직일 수가 없어.

speaker: MERCUTIO
raw:
You are a lover, borrow Cupid’s wings,
And soar with them above a common bound.

sentences.en: You are a lover, so borrow Cupid's wings and fly higher than ordinary men.
sentences.ko: 너는 연인이니 큐피드의 날개를 빌려 평범한 사람들보다 더 높이 날아올라 봐.

speaker: ROMEO
raw:
I am too sore enpierced with his shaft
To soar with his light feathers, and so bound,
I cannot bound a pitch above dull woe.
Under love’s heavy burden do I sink.

sentences.en: I am hurt too much by his arrow.
sentences.ko: 나는 그의 화살에 너무 깊은 상처를 입었어.

sentences.en: I cannot fly with his light feathers.
sentences.ko: 그의 가벼운 깃털로는 날 수 없어.

sentences.en: I am bound so tightly that I cannot jump above dull sadness.
sentences.ko: 너무 꽁꽁 묶여서 이 우울함 위로는 뛰어오를 수 없어.

sentences.en: I sink under the heavy burden of love.
sentences.ko: 사랑이라는 무거운 짐 아래로 가라앉고 있어.

speaker: MERCUTIO
raw:
And, to sink in it, should you burden love;
Too great oppression for a tender thing.

sentences.en: If you sink into love, you will be a heavy weight on it.
sentences.ko: 네가 사랑에 빠져 가라앉으면, 오히려 사랑에게 무거운 짐이 되는 거야.

sentences.en: It is too heavy a burden for such a delicate thing.
sentences.ko: 그렇게 섬세한 것에겐 너무 무거운 짐이야.

speaker: ROMEO
raw:
Is love a tender thing? It is too rough,
Too rude, too boisterous; and it pricks like thorn.

sentences.en: Is love a delicate thing?
sentences.ko: 사랑이 섬세한 것이라고?

sentences.en: No, it is too rough, wild, and loud, and it pricks like a thorn.
sentences.ko: 아니, 너무 거칠고 사납고 시끄러워. 가시처럼 찌르지.

speaker: MERCUTIO

sentences.en: If love is rough with you, be rough with love.
sentences.ko: 사랑이 너를 거칠게 대한다면, 너도 사랑을 거칠게 대해.

sentences.en: Prick love back for pricking you.
sentences.ko: 너를 찌르는 만큼 사랑도 똑같이 찔러버려.

sentences.en: Beat love down.
sentences.ko: 사랑을 때려눕혀 버려.

sentences.en: Give me a mask to hide my face in.
sentences.ko: 내 얼굴을 가릴 가면을 하나 줘.

raw: Putting on a mask.

sentences.en: Mercutio puts on a mask.
sentences.ko: 머큐쇼가 가면을 쓴다.

speaker: MERCUTIO
raw:
A visor for a visor. What care I
What curious eye doth quote deformities?
Here are the beetle-brows shall blush for me.

sentences.en: A mask for a mask.
sentences.ko: 가면 위에 가면이라!

sentences.en: I do not care what eyes see my flaws.
sentences.ko: 내 결점을 누가 보든 상관없어.

sentences.en: This mask with its big eyebrows will blush for me.
sentences.ko: 굵은 눈썹이 달린 이 가면이 나 대신 얼굴을 붉혀 줄 거야.

speaker: BENVOLIO
raw:
Come, knock and enter; and no sooner in
But every man betake him to his legs.

sentences.en: Come, knock and enter.
sentences.ko: 자, 두드리고 들어가자.

sentences.en: As soon as we are inside, every man should start dancing.
sentences.ko: 들어가자마자 모두 춤을 추는 거야.

speaker: ROMEO
raw:
A torch for me: let wantons, light of heart,
Tickle the senseless rushes with their heels;
For I am proverb’d with a grandsire phrase,
I’ll be a candle-holder and look on,
The game was ne’er so fair, and I am done.

sentences.en: Give me a torch.
sentences.ko: 횃불 하나 줘.

sentences.en: Let the light-hearted people dance on the straw-covered floor.
sentences.ko: 신이 난 사람들은 짚이 깔린 바닥에서 춤추게 해.

sentences.en: I am following an old saying.
sentences.ko: 나는 옛 속담을 따르는 것뿐이야.

sentences.en: I will be a candle-holder and watch.
sentences.ko: 난 촛대 들고 구경이나 할게.

sentences.en: It is best to quit while the game is good, so I am done.
sentences.ko: 분위기가 좋을 때 그만두는 게 좋으니, 난 여기까지야.

speaker: MERCUTIO
raw:
Tut, dun’s the mouse, the constable’s own word:
If thou art dun, we’ll draw thee from the mire
Or save your reverence love, wherein thou stickest
Up to the ears. Come, we burn daylight, ho.

sentences.en: Be quiet as a mouse, as the police say.
sentences.ko: 경찰 말처럼, 쥐 죽은 듯 조용히 해.

sentences.en: If you are stuck, we will pull you from the mud.
sentences.ko: 네가 진창에 빠졌다면 우리가 꺼내 줄게.

sentences.en: Or, to be polite, we will pull you out of the love you are stuck in.
sentences.ko: 아니, 예의를 차려 말하자면 네가 빠진 사랑에서 꺼내 주겠다는 뜻이야.

sentences.en: Come, we are wasting daylight.
sentences.ko: 자, 이러다 시간만 버리겠어.

speaker: ROMEO
raw: Nay, that’s not so.

sentences.en: No, that is not true.
sentences.ko: 아니, 그렇지 않아.

speaker: MERCUTIO
raw:
I mean sir, in delay
We waste our lights in vain, light lights by day.
Take our good meaning, for our judgment sits
Five times in that ere once in our five wits.

sentences.en: I mean, sir, we waste our energy by waiting.
sentences.ko: 내 말은, 기다리느라 에너지를 낭비하고 있다는 거야.

sentences.en: We are wasting our light in the daytime.
sentences.ko: 대낮에 등불을 켜는 셈이지.

sentences.en: Take what I mean, not my word games.
sentences.ko: 말장난이 아니라 내 의도를 알아들어.

sentences.en: Good sense is found more in what we mean than in our clever words.
sentences.ko: 지혜는 화려한 말보다 그 속에 담긴 뜻에서 나오는 법이야.

speaker: ROMEO
raw:
And we mean well in going to this mask;
But ’tis no wit to go.

sentences.en: We mean well by going to this masked party.
sentences.ko: 이 가면 무도회에 가는 건 좋은 의도에서 하는 일이야.

sentences.en: But it is not smart to go.
sentences.ko: 하지만 가는 게 현명한 일은 아니야.

speaker: MERCUTIO
raw: Why, may one ask?

sentences.en: May one ask why?
sentences.ko: 왜냐고 물어봐도 될까?

speaker: ROMEO
raw: I dreamt a dream tonight.

sentences.en: I had a dream tonight.
sentences.ko: 오늘 밤 꿈을 꿨어.

speaker: MERCUTIO
raw: And so did I.

sentences.en: So did I.
sentences.ko: 나도 그랬어.

speaker: ROMEO
raw: Well what was yours?

sentences.en: Well, what was your dream?
sentences.ko: 그래서, 어떤 꿈이었는데?

speaker: MERCUTIO
raw: That dreamers often lie.

sentences.en: That dreamers often lie.
sentences.ko: 꿈꾸는 사람들은 종종 거짓말을 한다는 거야.

speaker: ROMEO
raw: In bed asleep, while they do dream things true.

sentences.en: They lie in bed asleep, while they dream true things.
sentences.ko: 그들은 침대에 누워 잠든 채로, 진실한 꿈을 꾸지.

speaker: MERCUTIO
raw:
O, then, I see Queen Mab hath been with you.
She is the fairies’ midwife, and she comes
In shape no bigger than an agate-stone
On the fore-finger of an alderman,
Drawn with a team of little atomies
Over men’s noses as they lie asleep:
Her waggon-spokes made of long spinners’ legs;
The cover, of the wings of grasshoppers;
Her traces, of the smallest spider’s web;
The collars, of the moonshine’s watery beams;
Her whip of cricket’s bone; the lash, of film;
Her waggoner, a small grey-coated gnat,
Not half so big as a round little worm
Prick’d from the lazy finger of a maid:
Her chariot is an empty hazelnut,
Made by the joiner squirrel or old grub,
Time out o’ mind the fairies’ coachmakers.
And in this state she gallops night by night
Through lovers’ brains, and then they dream of love;
O’er courtiers’ knees, that dream on curtsies straight;
O’er lawyers’ fingers, who straight dream on fees;
O’er ladies’ lips, who straight on kisses dream,
Which oft the angry Mab with blisters plagues,
Because their breaths with sweetmeats tainted are:
Sometime she gallops o’er a courtier’s nose,
And then dreams he of smelling out a suit;
And sometime comes she with a tithe-pig’s tail,
Tickling a parson’s nose as a lies asleep,
Then dreams he of another benefice:
Sometime she driveth o’er a soldier’s neck,
And then dreams he of cutting foreign throats,
Of breaches, ambuscados, Spanish blades,
Of healths five fathom deep; and then anon
Drums in his ear, at which he starts and wakes;
And, being thus frighted, swears a prayer or two,
And sleeps again. This is that very Mab
That plats the manes of horses in the night;
And bakes the elf-locks in foul sluttish hairs,
Which, once untangled, much misfortune bodes:
This is the hag, when maids lie on their backs,
That presses them, and learns them first to bear,
Making them women of good carriage:
This is she,—

sentences.en: Then I see Queen Mab has been with you.
sentences.ko: 그렇다면 맵 여왕이 너를 찾아왔나 보군.

sentences.en: She is the midwife of the fairies.
sentences.ko: 그녀는 요정들의 산파야.

sentences.en: She is no bigger than the small stone in a ring on an old councilman's finger.
sentences.ko: 늙은 시의원 손가락에 낀 반지의 작은 보석보다도 크지 않아.

sentences.en: She is pulled by a team of tiny creatures.
sentences.ko: 아주 작은 생물들이 그녀의 마차를 끌어.

sentences.en: They pull her over men's noses while they sleep.
sentences.ko: 그들은 잠든 사람들의 코 위로 그녀를 끌고 가.

sentences.en: Her wagon wheels are made of long spiders' legs.
sentences.ko: 그녀의 마차 바퀴는 긴 거미 다리로 만들어졌어.

sentences.en: The cover is made of grasshopper wings.
sentences.ko: 덮개는 메뚜기 날개로 만들었지.

sentences.en: Her reins are made of the smallest spider's web.
sentences.ko: 고삐는 아주 가는 거미줄로 만들었어.

sentences.en: The collars are made of moonbeams.
sentences.ko: 말의 목줄은 달빛으로 만들었고.

sentences.en: Her whip is made of cricket bone.
sentences.ko: 채찍은 귀뚜라미 뼈로 만들었어.

sentences.en: The lash is made of thin film.
sentences.ko: 채찍 끝은 얇은 막으로 되어 있어.

sentences.en: Her driver is a small grey-coated gnat.
sentences.ko: 마부는 회색 옷을 입은 작은 각다귀야.

sentences.en: He is not even as big as a round little worm.
sentences.ko: 그는 동그랗고 작은 벌레보다도 작아.

sentences.en: The worm was pricked from the lazy finger of an unmarried girl.
sentences.ko: 게으른 처녀의 손가락에서 파낸 벌레 말이야.

sentences.en: Her chariot is an empty hazelnut.
sentences.ko: 그녀의 마차는 빈 헤이즐넛이야.

sentences.en: It was made by a squirrel or a bug.
sentences.ko: 다람쥐나 벌레가 만든 거지.

sentences.en: They have been the fairies' coachmakers since ancient times.
sentences.ko: 그들은 아주 오래전부터 요정들의 마차 제작자였어.

sentences.en: In this state, she gallops night by night through lovers' brains.
sentences.ko: 이렇게 그녀는 밤마다 연인들의 머릿속을 달리지.

sentences.en: Then they dream of love.
sentences.ko: 그러면 그들은 사랑에 대한 꿈을 꾸지.

sentences.en: She rides over the knees of royal officials.
sentences.ko: 그녀는 고위 관리들의 무릎 위를 지나가.

sentences.en: They dream of bowing to others.
sentences.ko: 그들은 남들에게 절하는 꿈을 꿔.

sentences.en: She rides over lawyers' fingers.
sentences.ko: 그녀는 변호사들의 손가락 위를 지나가.

sentences.en: They dream about their fees.
sentences.ko: 그들은 수임료에 관한 꿈을 꾸지.

sentences.en: She rides over ladies' lips.
sentences.ko: 그녀는 여인들의 입술 위를 지나가.

sentences.en: They dream of kisses.
sentences.ko: 그들은 키스에 대한 꿈을 꿔.

sentences.en: The angry Mab often punishes them with blisters.
sentences.ko: 화난 맵은 종종 그들의 입술에 물집을 내 벌을 줘.

sentences.en: This is because their breath smells like sweets.
sentences.ko: 숨결에서 단내가 나기 때문이야.

sentences.en: Sometimes she gallops over an official's nose.
sentences.ko: 때때로 그녀는 관리의 코 위를 지나가.

sentences.en: Then he dreams of someone who will pay him for a favor.
sentences.ko: 그러면 그는 부탁을 들어주는 대가로 돈을 줄 사람에 대한 꿈을 꿔.

sentences.en: Sometimes she comes with a pig's tail.
sentences.ko: 가끔은 돼지 꼬리를 들고 와.

sentences.en: She tickles a priest's nose while he sleeps.
sentences.ko: 그녀는 잠든 신부의 코를 간지럽히지.

sentences.en: Then he dreams of another church job with more pay.
sentences.ko: 그러면 그는 더 많은 급여를 받는 다른 교회 직무에 관한 꿈을 꿔.

sentences.en: Sometimes she rides over a soldier's neck.
sentences.ko: 때때로 그녀는 군인의 목 위를 지나가.

sentences.en: Then he dreams of cutting foreign throats.
sentences.ko: 그러면 그는 외국인의 목을 베는 꿈을 꿔.

sentences.en: He dreams of battles and Spanish blades.
sentences.ko: 그는 전투와 스페인 칼들에 대한 꿈을 꾸지.

sentences.en: He dreams of drinking huge toasts.
sentences.ko: 그는 큰 잔을 들어 마시는 꿈을 꿔.

sentences.en: Then suddenly drums sound in his ear.
sentences.ko: 그러다 갑자기 그의 귀에 북소리가 들려.

sentences.en: He starts and wakes up.
sentences.ko: 그는 깜짝 놀라 깨어나.

sentences.en: Because he is scared, he says a prayer or two.
sentences.ko: 무서워진 그는 기도 한두 번을 올리지.

sentences.en: Then he falls asleep again.
sentences.ko: 그러고 나서 다시 잠이 들어.

sentences.en: This is the same Mab who braids horse hair at night.
sentences.ko: 밤마다 말갈기를 땋는 것도 바로 그 맵이야.

sentences.en: She tangles dirty hair into knots called elf-locks.
sentences.ko: 그녀는 지저분한 머리카락을 엉켜 '엘프 록'이라 불리는 매듭으로 만들어.

sentences.en: If that hair is untangled, it means bad luck.
sentences.ko: 그 엉킨 머리를 풀면 불운이 온대.

sentences.en: This is the hag who visits unmarried girls while they lie on their backs.
sentences.ko: 이건 미혼 소녀들이 등을 대고 누워 있을 때 찾아오는 노파야.

sentences.en: She presses down on them and teaches them to bear a man's weight.
sentences.ko: 그녀는 그들을 짓누르며 남자의 무게를 견디는 법을 가르쳐.

sentences.en: That makes them women who will carry children well.
sentences.ko: 그렇게 해서 아이를 잘 품는 여자가 되는 거지.

sentences.en: This is she—
sentences.ko: 그게 바로 그녀—

speaker: ROMEO
raw:
Peace, peace, Mercutio, peace,
Thou talk’st of nothing.

sentences.en: Peace, peace, Mercutio, peace.
sentences.ko: 그만, 그만해, 머큐쇼, 그만.

sentences.en: You are talking about nothing.
sentences.ko: 넌 아무 의미 없는 소리를 하고 있어.

speaker: MERCUTIO
raw:
True, I talk of dreams,
Which are the children of an idle brain,
Begot of nothing but vain fantasy,
Which is as thin of substance as the air,
And more inconstant than the wind, who woos
Even now the frozen bosom of the north,
And, being anger’d, puffs away from thence,
Turning his side to the dew-dropping south.

sentences.en: True, I talk of dreams.
sentences.ko: 맞아, 난 꿈에 대해 말하고 있지.

sentences.en: Dreams are the children of an idle brain.
sentences.ko: 꿈은 한가한 정신이 낳은 자식이야.

sentences.en: They come from nothing but useless fantasy.
sentences.ko: 그저 헛된 공상에서 나오는 거야.

sentences.en: Fantasy is as thin as the air.
sentences.ko: 환상은 공기만큼이나 가벼워.

sentences.en: It is more unstable than the wind.
sentences.ko: 그건 바람보다 더 불안정해.

sentences.en: The wind tries to kiss the frozen heart of the north.
sentences.ko: 바람은 얼어붙은 북쪽의 심장에 입맞춤을 하려 해.

sentences.en: Then, getting angry, it blows away from there.
sentences.ko: 그러다 화가 나서 그곳에서 멀리 날아가 버리지.

sentences.en: It turns toward the wet south.
sentences.ko: 그리고는 젖은 남쪽으로 향해.

speaker: BENVOLIO
raw:
This wind you talk of blows us from ourselves:
Supper is done, and we shall come too late.

sentences.en: This wind you talk about distracts us.
sentences.ko: 네가 말하는 그 바람이 우리를 딴 데로 날려 보내고 있어.

sentences.en: Dinner is finished.
sentences.ko: 저녁 식사는 벌써 끝났고.

sentences.en: We will arrive too late.
sentences.ko: 이러다 너무 늦겠어.

speaker: ROMEO
raw:
I fear too early: for my mind misgives
Some consequence yet hanging in the stars,
Shall bitterly begin his fearful date
With this night’s revels; and expire the term
Of a despised life, clos’d in my breast
By some vile forfeit of untimely death.
But he that hath the steerage of my course
Direct my suit. On, lusty gentlemen!

sentences.en: I fear it is too early.
sentences.ko: 난 너무 이를까 봐 걱정이야.

sentences.en: My mind fears a consequence in the stars.
sentences.ko: 아직 별 속에 걸려 있는 어떤 일이 두려워.

sentences.en: It may start with this night's party.
sentences.ko: 그건 오늘 밤 파티에서 시작될지도 몰라.

sentences.en: It might end my life quickly.
sentences.ko: 그게 내 생명을 순식간에 끝낼 수도 있어.

sentences.en: Death could take my life before its time.
sentences.ko: 죽음이 내 수명을 채우기도 전에 앗아갈 수도 있거든.

sentences.en: But let him who controls my path guide me.
sentences.ko: 하지만 내 앞길의 키를 쥔 분이 나를 이끄시기를.

sentences.en: Let us go, brave gentlemen!
sentences.ko: 가자, 용감한 신사들이여!

speaker: BENVOLIO
raw: Strike, drum.

sentences.en: Beat the drum.
sentences.ko: 북을 쳐라.

raw: Exeunt.
